chunks: They have no knowledge of this, nor their fathers. How great is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak nothing but lies.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about those who claim knowledge without basis?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to critique blind imitation (taqlid) of ancestors or scholars when it lacks grounding in true knowledge or divine revelation. It underscores the gravity of speaking without basis, characterizing such empty assertions as pure falsehood, a theme resonating with the concept of 'Ilm al-Yaqin' (knowledge of certainty) versus mere opinion.
